newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian expert says IMF unlikely to delay tranche.
newsitem.headline: Russian expert says IMF unlikely to delay tranche.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is unlikely to delay the September tranche of its $10 billion loan to Russia, a finance ministry expert said on Friday.
"We have no problems with quantitative indicators," said Jochen Wermuth, head of the Economic Expert Group at the finance ministry. "Now we are discussing only structural reforms."
IMF experts visit Russia every month to monitor economic performance under a programme backed by the loan, and the money is paid out in monthly tranches.
The fund looks at specific indicators -- money supply, the budget deficit, and foreign reserves -- as well as general progress in economic reform.

Wermuth said the latest mission, which visited Moscow for three days this month, had not had time to receive all the necessary data, and there would be further discussions at the IMF/World Bank meetings in Washington next week.

Wermuth told a news conference that restructuring the Russian economy was the main problem facing the IMF. "Before the elections these reforms were not implemented as they should have been," Wermuth said.
But after the June/July presidential election the government had redoubled its efforts in carrying out structural reforms.
The IMF delayed payment of the July tranche of the loan because of concern over the budget deficit. The money was eventually paid.
